question: A dishonest shopkeeper claims that he sells rock salt at ₹17/kg, which costs him 20/kg. But he gives 567 g instead of 1134 g. What is his profit percentage?
solution:
**Given:**

Cost price per kg = ₹20

ng price per kg = ₹17

Weight sold = 567 g instead of 1134 g

**Formula used:**

Profit Percentage = dfrac{{Profit}}{{Cost Price}} times 100

Profit = Selling Price - Effective Cost Price

Effective Cost Price = Cost Price × Actual Weight Sold / Claimed Weight

**Calculation:**

Effective Cost Price = ₹20 × dfrac{567}{1134}

⇒ Effective Cost Price = ₹20 × 0.5

⇒ Effective Cost Price = ₹10

Profit = Selling Price - Effective Cost Price

⇒ Profit = ₹17 - ₹10

⇒ Profit = ₹7

Profit Percentage = dfrac{7}{10} times 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = 70%

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**
